questions.q: What concern did Jesus state about the great crowd that had been following him?
questions.a: Jesus stated that he was concerned the great crowd had nothing to eat.

questions.q: How many loaves did the disciples have with them?
questions.a: The disciples had seven loaves with them.

questions.q: What did Jesus do with the disciples’ loaves?
questions.a: Jesus gave thanks, broke the loaves, and gave them to his disciples to serve.

questions.q: How much food remained after everyone had eaten?
questions.a: There were seven baskets of food remaining after everyone had eaten.

questions.q: How many people ate and were satisfied?
questions.a: There were about 4,000 men who ate and were satisfied.

questions.q: To test him, what did the Pharisees want Jesus to do?
questions.a: The Pharisees wanted Jesus to give them a sign from heaven.

questions.q: About what did Jesus warn his disciples concerning the Pharisees?
questions.a: Jesus warned his disciples to be on guard against the yeast of the Pharisees.

questions.q: About what did the disciples think Jesus was talking?
questions.a: The disciples thought Jesus was talking about the fact that they had forgotten to bring bread.

questions.q: Jesus reminded his disciples that what had happened when Jesus had broken five loaves?
questions.a: Jesus reminded them that when he had broken five loaves, 5,000 people had been fed and 12 baskets full of broken pieces had been taken up.

questions.q: What two things did Jesus first do to the blind man in order to restore his sight?
questions.a: Jesus first spat on his eyes and laid his hands upon him.

questions.q: What third thing did Jesus do to the blind man in order to completely restore his sight?
questions.a: Jesus laid his hands upon his eyes again.

questions.q: Who were the people saying that Jesus was?
questions.a: The people were saying that Jesus was John the Baptizer, Elijah, or one of the prophets.

questions.q: Who did Peter say that Jesus was?
questions.a: Peter said that Jesus was the Christ.

questions.q: About what future events did Jesus begin to teach his disciples clearly?
questions.a: Jesus taught his disciples that the Son of Man must suffer, be rejected, be killed, and be raised after three days.

questions.q: What did Jesus say when Peter began to rebuke him?
questions.a: Jesus said to Peter, “Get behind me Satan! You do not care for the things of God, but for the things of people.”

questions.q: What did Jesus say anyone who wants to follow him must do?
questions.a: Jesus said that anyone who wants to follow him must deny himself, take up his cross, and follow Jesus.

questions.q: What did Jesus say about a person’s desire to gain the things of the world?
questions.a: Jesus said, “What does it profit a person to gain the whole world and then forfeit his life?”

questions.q: What did Jesus say he would do concerning those who are ashamed of him and his words?
questions.a: Jesus said that at his coming he would be ashamed of those who were ashamed of him and his words.

commentary.text: Four thousand fed by a miracle.
Christ cautions against the Pharisees and Herodians.

Verses 1–10 Our Lord Jesus encouraged the meanest to come to him for life and grace. Christ knows and considers our frames. The bounty of Christ is always ready; to show that, he repeated this miracle. His favours are renewed, as our wants and necessities are. And those need not fear want, who have Christ to live upon by faith, and do so with thanksgiving.

Obstinate unbelief will have something to say, though ever so unreasonable. Christ refused to answer their demand. If they will not be convinced, they shall not. Alas! what cause we have to lament for those around us, who destroy themselves and others by their perverse and obstinate unbelief, and enmity to the gospel! When we forget the works of God, and distrust him, we should chide ourselves severely, as Christ here reproves his disciples. How is it that we so often mistake his meaning, disregard his warnings, and distrust his providence?

Here is a blind man brought to Christ by his friends. Therein appeared the faith of those that brought him. If those who are spiritually blind, do not pray for themselves, yet their friends and relations should pray for them, that Christ would be pleased to touch them. The cure was wrought gradually, which was not usual in our Lord's miracles. Christ showed in what method those commonly are healed by his grace, who by nature are spiritually blind. At first, their knowledge is confused; but, like the light of the morning, it shines more and more to the perfect day, and then they see all things clearly. Slighting Christ's favours is forfeiting them; and he will make those who do so know the worth of privileges by the want of them.

These things are written, that we may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God. These miracles of our Lord assure us that he was not conquered, but a Conqueror. Now the disciples are convinced that Jesus is the Christ; they may bear to hear of his sufferings, of which Christ here begins to give them notice. He sees that amiss in what we say and do, of which we ourselves are not aware, and knows what manner of spirit we are of, when we ourselves do not. The wisdom of man is folly, when it pretends to limit the Divine counsels. Peter did not rightly understand the nature of Christ's kingdom.

Frequent notice is taken of the great flocking there was to Christ for help in various cases. All are concerned to know this, if they expect him to heal their souls. They must not indulge the ease of the body. As the happiness of heaven with Christ, is enough to make up for the loss of life itself for him, so the gain of all the world in sin, will not make up for the ruin of the soul by sin. And there is a day coming, when the cause of Christ will appear as glorious, as some now think it mean and contemptible. May we think of that season, and view every earthly object as we shall do at that great day.
